Of course. Here is an introduction to Horsehead Corporation that is over 200 words.

***

Horsehead Corporation, a name that was once synonymous with American industrial might and metallurgical innovation, operated for decades as a pivotal player in the North American zinc industry from its sprawling headquarters at 300 Frankfort Road in Monaca, Pennsylvania. With a legacy stretching back to the 19th century through its predecessor, the New Jersey Zinc Company, Horsehead grew to become a dominant force in zinc production and, most notably, in environmental services through the recycling of hazardous industrial waste. The company’s very name was a nod to its industrial heritage, derived from the unique, horse-head-shaped formations of zinc residue that were a byproduct of a historic smelting process.

At the core of its modern business model was the processing of Electric Arc Furnace (EAF) dust, a zinc-rich waste material generated by steel mini-mills. Horsehead pioneered and scaled a process to reclaim valuable zinc from this dust, transforming a hazardous liability for steelmakers into a valuable raw material. This made the Monaca plant not just a smelting facility but one of the largest recyclers of its kind in the world, positioning the company as both a chemical producer and an environmental solutions provider. For the community of Monaca and the greater Beaver County region, the Frankfort Road plant was a crucial economic engine, providing thousands of jobs over generations. However, the company's story is also marked by significant financial and operational challenges, which ultimately led to its bankruptcy in 2016 and the eventual closure of the historic Monaca site, leaving behind a complex legacy of industrial innovation, economic impact, and environmental responsibility.
